body.statement: For every \(z>0\), the limiting coverage of the conventional selected interval is \(C_z(k)\). At an exact selector tie, \(C_z(0)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for all \(\rho_1,\rho_2\in[-1,1]\). For any fixed \(z>0\), \(C_z(k)=2\Phi(z)-1\) for every \(k\in\mathbb R\) if and only if \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\). If \(k\neq0\) and \(\rho_1^2\neq\rho_2^2\), then \(\operatorname{sign}\{C_z(k)-[2\Phi(z)-1]\}=\operatorname{sign}\{k(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2)\}\).
body.justification: The coverage function separates harmless selected asymmetry from genuine two-sided Wald distortion and gives its strict direction.
body.gap: Leeb, Pötscher, and Ewald give comparator-specific Gaussian coverage formulas, and Azzalini--Regoli give even-functional symmetry; neither gives this selected-coordinate all-gap if-and-only-if boundary.
body.consumer: The equality \(\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2\) is a feasible robustness diagnostic for deciding whether conventional role-selected intervals require correction.
